2: An idolater who holds a feast for their son’s or daughter’s wedding—it is forbidden for an Israelite to eat there, even if they eat their own food and their own servant stands by and serves them. From when is it forbidden? From the time preparations for the feast begin and for 30 days after the wedding feast. If the idolater says they are inviting [the Israelite] specifically for the wedding, it is forbidden until 12 months have passed. After 12 months, it is permitted unless the idolater is a distinguished person.
If the idolater holding the wedding sends live poultry or fish to the Israelite’s home, it is permitted [to accept and eat them].
